q-20413.name: Question 1
q-20413.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14123219/assets/4bb7598c9ebae28be572508974cd025caa8f4a6c3313f025ff0f5ca55296334e.png)

Consider the picture above. Given that $h=\lambda f+\mu g$, find $\lambda $ and $\mu .$
q-20413.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14123219/assets/43642acdb991827b4e1e16744e8a69507a383a1319ae07efde78480af4bab166.png)

In $△OFH$ shown above, we have 

- $OF=2|g|$

- $\overset{\to }{OF}$ and $g$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OF}=2g.$

Similarly:

- $FH=3|f|$

- $\overset{\to }{FH}$ has the opposite direction to $f$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{FH}=-3f.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}h & =\overset{\to }{OF}+\overset{\to }{FH} \\  & =2g-3f \\  & =-3f+2g.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $h=\lambda f+\mu g=-3f+2g.$

Since $f∦g,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =-3$ and $\mu =2$

q-20413.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the picture above. Given that h=λf+μg, find λ and μ.

a
λ=1 and μ=2
b
λ=2 and μ=−3
c
λ=−3 and μ=2
d
λ=−3 and μ=3
e
λ=3 and μ=2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In △OFH shown above, we have

  • OF=2|g|
  • OF→ and g have the same direction

Hence, OF→=2g.

Similarly:

  • FH=3|f|
  • FH→ has the opposite direction to f

Hence, FH→=−3f.

Additionally,

h=OF→+FH→=2g−3f=−3f+2g.

Consequently, h=λf+μg=−3f+2g.

Since f∦g, the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

  • λ=−3 and μ=2

q-77230.name: Question 2
q-77230.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14123219/assets/8cf7d0520b1d0654d5749651595acd48b7a08f2b2d55142b18ca63b2ded20f55.png)

Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a+2b$, find $\lambda .$
q-77230.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+2b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $2b.$ So, we first draw the vector $2b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14123219/assets/9edea1e3ad727d11d7bfac884f27c1b435233fa7df561dbe2a4f3af45ea16bfa.png)

In $△OBC$, we have:

- $BC=3|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{BC}$ and $a$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{BC}=3a.$ 

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OB}+\overset{\to }{BC} \\  & =2b+3a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=2b+\lambda a=2b+3a.$ 

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a$, we get:

$$
\lambda =3
$$

q-120289.name: Question 3
q-120289.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14123219/assets/52e25ccc5b59b3eecd914c5b141e443475a5de58299404528d27f1fc85db97ea.png)

Consider the diagram above, where $\overset{\to }{OA}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{OB}=b$, and $T$ divides $\overset{―}{AB}$ in the ratio $AT:TB=3:5.$ Find $\overset{\to }{OT}.$
q-120289.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that

$$
\overset{\to }{OT}=\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AT}.
$$

We're told that $\overset{\to }{OA}=a,$ so we just need to work out $\overset{\to }{AT}.$

First, from $△OAB,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{AO}+\overset{\to }{OB} \\  & =-\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{OB} \\  & =-a+b \\  & =b-a.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $AT:TB=3:5,$ we have

$$
\overset{\to }{AT}=\frac{3}{8}\overset{\to }{AB}=\frac{3}{8}(b-a).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OT} & =\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AT} \\  & =a+\frac{3}{8}(b-a) \\  & =\frac{5}{8}a+\frac{3}{8}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the diagram above, where OA→=a, OB→=b, and T divides AB― in the ratio AT:TB=3:5. Find OT→.

a
OT→=78a+18b
b
OT→=58a+38b
c
OT→=34a+14b
d
OT→=38a+58b
e
OT→=14a+34b
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the diagram, we see that OT→=OA→+AT→.

We're told that OA→=a, so we just need to work out AT→.

First, from △OAB, we have

AB→=AO→+OB→=−OA→+OB→=−a+b=b−a.

Since AT:TB=3:5, we have

AT→=38AB→=38(b−a).

Therefore,

OT→=OA→+AT→=a+38(b−a)=58a+38b.
